correctness.rationale: With \(N\) nonzero e-values, base e-BH rejects under the complete null exactly when \(Nc\ge K/\alpha\), so FDR is the corresponding binomial tail. For fixed \(p>0\) validity makes \(c=1/p\) worst, and partitioning \(p\) by the integer rejection threshold reduces the exact envelope to \(\max_r \Pr\{\mathrm{Bin}(K,r\alpha/K)\ge r\}\). For \(r\ge2\), the factorial-moment inequality bounds the tail by \((e\alpha)^r\), whereas the \(r=1\) term is at least \(\alpha-\alpha^2/2\); the stated \(\alpha_0\) makes the latter strictly larger. The equality constraints also force the unique law \(p=\alpha/K,c=K/\alpha\). Independent recomputation for several levels and sample sizes reproduced the envelope and the one-spike optimizer.

value.rationale: All-or-nothing e-values are a canonical sharpness family in the foundational e-BH paper. The result quantifies exactly how independence changes that sharpness picture and identifies a unique extremizer at standard FDR levels, giving a useful calibration benchmark rather than a routine numerical example.

limitations: Complete null, iid two-point e-values only.
The displayed \(\alpha_0\) is a sufficient optimizer range, not claimed to be the largest possible range.
